test_title: PYST 3: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

He took such an offense at the remark (1)/ that he refused to speak with the manager (2)/ despite repeated requests made (3)/ on behalf of the HR department. (4)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is located in **part (1)** of the sentence.
 
• The phrase "**take offense**" is an established idiom that means to feel resentful, hurt, or insulted by something.
 
• In this context, the word "offense" functions as an uncountable noun representing a feeling or emotional state, so it should not be preceded by the indefinite article "**an**."
 
• Therefore, the article "**an**" must be removed to correct the phrase to "took such offense."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He took **such offense** at the remark that he refused to speak with the manager despite repeated requests made on behalf of the HR department."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: (2) **– This part is grammatically correct. The construction "refused to speak" properly uses the infinitive form of the verb.
 
• **Option 3: (3)** – This part is grammatically correct. The phrase "despite repeated requests made" correctly uses the preposition "despite" followed by a noun phrase.
 
• **Option 4: (4)** – This part is grammatically correct. The idiom "on behalf of" properly indicates that the requests were made representing the HR department.
